sentences.text: A woodpecker smashes its head into a tree over and over.
Why doesn't it get a concussion?
Many people assumed its skull works like a shock absorber.
But when scientists filmed woodpeckers in slow motion, the head stopped hard, like a hammer.
Cushioning would only weaken each peck.
A woodpecker's brain is tiny, and the same jolt creates far less pressure inside a small brain.
